tool_args.rationale: The thermal-fin bridge and flux-conservation signatures point toward the inland-hub siphon family, but the pilot varies only u_now. The open-branch probe can distinguish sink-gradient dependence and branch terms before fitting and confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the thermal-fin bridge siphon model directly
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: All five pilot rows have the same sink gradient, so the sink coefficient and branch behavior are not identifiable from the pilot alone.

considered_alternatives.option: Cooperative Hill or barrier-modulated siphon models
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: These are plausible competing nonlinear mechanisms, but the fixed-gradient pilot cannot discriminate their sink dependence.
The pilot signature and saturation pattern favor a static bridge-flux mechanism; a trajectory batch is less targeted than varying the sink gradient.
It is not relevant to the identified ambiguity.
